disclosures.said: Only the solid coloured boxes that carry a tag are things I am asking about. The thin dashed lines you may see on some pictures are marks left over in the pictures themselves; disregard them.
About screen 24: that picture was taken before the middle of the page had finished drawing; on the running app that middle area shows the same thing as on screen 8.
(there is no 13 and no 29 for you — skip those numbers)

screen1-a1.where: Top right corner, the first of the two small pictures beside the words 'PDF Reader' - a little gold crown with a red jewel.
screen1-a1.expectation: I do not know. A crown might mean something special or something I would have to pay for, but that is a guess.
screen1-a1.cue: Only the picture of a crown. There is no word with it.

first_pass.why: A crown is not a symbol I know on a telephone. I would have to work out what it means, and whatever I worked out today I would not remember tomorrow, so I would not press it.
first_pass.solution: Put a plain word under or beside it, such as 'Upgrade' or 'Buy the full version', so I know before I press it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the crown shows what it is for, and whether the picture would tell you next time
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the crown picture at the top right. Look at what opens (do NOT press "Start Free Trial"). Then close that page with the X at its top left, and look at the crown again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the gold crown at the top right of the main page. After a short wait a full page came up with a large jewel picture and the heading 'Try the Premium plan completely free', a list for Today, Day 2 and Day 3, and a big 'Start Free Trial' button, which I did not touch. So the crown is the door to paying for the full version. I closed the page with the X at its top left and was back on the main page. The crown looked exactly as before: a gold crown, no word. Having seen the page, I know today what it means. But nothing on the crown itself would tell me next time, and I will not carry today's visit with me.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: Pressing it did tell me - it is the way to pay for the full version - but the crown itself still carries no word. Next time I shall be exactly where I started, looking at a crown and not knowing. A word such as 'Upgrade' beside it is still what I need.

screen1-a2.where: Top right corner, the second small picture - a black cog wheel with a spanner across it.
screen1-a2.expectation: Probably the settings for this programme, where I change how it works.
screen1-a2.cue: The cog wheel looks something like the settings picture on my own telephone, but the spanner across it makes it a different picture from the one I know.

first_pass.why: A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it.
first_pass.solution: Write the word 'Settings' under it, and use the same plain cog as the rest of my telephone.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the cog-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened headed 'Settings', with a back arrow, 'Upgrade to Premium', 'Keep screen on', 'Language', 'Set default reader', 'Add widget', 'Rate App', 'Share App', 'Privacy Policy' and 'Terms of Use'. I went back with the arrow at its top left. Then I pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar, and a different page opened with headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' and tiles such as 'Scan to PDF' and 'Merge PDF'. They are two plainly different places, and the cog's page is named 'Settings' at the top.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: The cog led to a page plainly headed 'Settings', and 'Tools' led somewhere quite different. So pressing it is safe and the heading tells me where I am once I arrive. I still could not be sure before pressing, because the picture has a spanner added and no word, so it remains a small difficulty rather than none.

screen1-a3.where: The row of rounded buttons under 'PDF Reader', the first one, reading 'PDF'.
screen1-a3.expectation: It would show me my PDF documents.
screen1-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' on it, and the name of the programme is 'PDF Reader'.

first_pass.why: PDF is a word I used for years in practice, and it is the name of the programme itself.

screen1-a4.where: The row of rounded buttons under 'PDF Reader', the second one, reading 'HWP'.
screen1-a4.expectation: I have no idea. Some other kind of file, perhaps.
screen1-a4.cue: Only the letters 'HWP', which mean nothing to me.

first_pass.why: 'HWP' is a set of initials I have never met. I cannot learn a new abbreviation and keep it, so this button is simply closed to me.
first_pass.solution: Spell it out in ordinary words, for example the full name of the kind of document it means, or leave it out if few people need it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing "HWP" tells you what HWP is
test_cases.action: On the main page, press "HWP" in the row of file types near the top. Look at the whole screen for anything that tells you what HWP is. Then press "PDF" to put it back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what HWP means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in plain words what HWP files are
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'HWP' in the row near the top. The button turned blue and so did the 'SET' button and the little book on the grey strip. Nothing else changed. The picture and 'To continue, please allow file access on your device' stayed as they were. Nowhere on the screen was there a word explaining what HWP is. I pressed 'PDF' afterwards and it turned red again.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: Pressing 'HWP' only changed the colour. Nothing anywhere told me what HWP means. It stays closed to me.

screen1-a5.where: The row of rounded buttons under 'PDF Reader', the third one, reading 'Word'.
screen1-a5.expectation: It would show me my Word documents - letters and the like.
screen1-a5.cue: The word 'Word', which I know from the office computer, sitting in a row with 'PDF' and 'Excel'.

first_pass.why: It is the name of the programme I wrote letters in for years; I know it.

screen1-a6.where: The row of rounded buttons under 'PDF Reader', the fourth one, reading 'Excel'.
screen1-a6.expectation: It would show me my Excel files - the tables of figures.
screen1-a6.cue: The word 'Excel', which I know from the office.

first_pass.why: Familiar name from my working life.

screen1-a7.where: The row of rounded buttons under 'PDF Reader', the last one on the right, reading 'PPT'.
screen1-a7.expectation: Perhaps the slide presentations - PowerPoint - but I am not sure the letters mean that.
screen1-a7.cue: Only the letters 'PPT'. I had to reach for what they might stand for.

first_pass.why: The others in the row are whole words I know; this one is initials. I might puzzle it out, but I would not trust my puzzling, and I would not remember it next time.
first_pass.solution: Write the ordinary name, 'PowerPoint' or 'Slides', instead of the initials.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing "PPT" tells you what PPT is
test_cases.action: On the main page, press "PPT" in the row of file types near the top. Look for anything that tells you in ordinary words what PPT is. Then press "PDF" to put it back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what PPT means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in ordinary words what PPT files are
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'PPT'. The button turned orange, as did 'SET' and the little book. The rest of the page stayed the same, with the same picture and the same request to allow file access. Nothing said 'PowerPoint' or 'slides' or anything else in ordinary words. I pressed 'PDF' to put it back; the page went blank for a moment and then came back as before with 'PDF' in red.

screen1-a7.closing_comment: Pressing 'PPT' changed the colour and nothing else. No ordinary word appeared. I am still left guessing at initials.

screen1-a8.where: Just below the row of buttons, at the very left of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very faint small 'x' in the corner and a red open-book picture.
screen1-a8.expectation: The small 'x' would probably close this grey strip. The red book I think is only a decoration.
screen1-a8.cue: A faint 'x' in the corner, which usually means close. But the box also holds the book picture, so I am not sure which part I am pressing.

first_pass.why: An 'x' for close is familiar to me, but this one is so faint and small I nearly missed it, and it is mixed up with a picture of a book that does not say what it does.
first_pass.solution: Make the 'x' clearly visible, or put the word 'Close' or 'No thanks' there, apart from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: On the main page I pressed the small faint x at the far left of the grey strip 'Set as default reader'. The strip simply went away. Nothing opened, nothing else changed, and the rest of the page moved up slightly. I had pressed the right thing and it did what I thought.

screen1-a8.closing_comment: The little x did exactly what I expected and nothing more - the strip went away. The book picture beside it did not get in the way. My only remaining complaint is that the x is very faint and tiny, and that is about seeing it, not about what it does.

screen1-a9.where: On the right of the grey strip, a coloured button reading 'SET', beside the words 'Set as default reader'.
screen1-a9.expectation: It would make this programme the one my telephone always uses to open my documents.
screen1-a9.cue: The sentence right beside it, 'Set as default reader', and the word 'SET' on the button.

first_pass.why: The sentence is right there next to the button, in ordinary words, and does not disappear.

screen1-a10.where: In the middle of the screen, a large black button reading 'Allow Access', under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.'
screen1-a10.expectation: It would give the programme permission to see the files on my telephone, so it can show me my documents.
screen1-a10.cue: The sentence directly above it and the words 'Allow Access' on the button.

first_pass.why: The instruction is written plainly just above the button and stays there. I know what I am agreeing to.

screen1-a11.where: Near the bottom right corner, above the row of buttons, a round black button with four white corner marks in it, like the corners of a frame.
screen1-a11.expectation: I have no idea. Possibly something to do with the camera, but that is a guess from nothing.
screen1-a11.cue: Nothing - only four corner marks. There is no word.

first_pass.why: I do not recognise this picture at all. I would have to work out what it means, and I cannot hold on to that. I would leave it alone.
first_pass.solution: Put a word on it or under it - 'Scan a paper document', if that is what it does.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. Look at what appears. Do NOT give any permission: if a box appears, close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. After a moment the page darkened and a white box came up: 'Request permission to access all files - To read and edit your document files, please allow PDF Reader, PDF Viewer to access all your files', with one button 'GO TO SET'. Nothing in it said what the round button itself was for - no mention of scanning, a camera or anything else. I closed it with the phone's Back key without giving any permission.

screen1-a11.closing_comment: I hoped pressing it would at least show me what it does. Instead it produced a general request for permission to all my files, which says nothing about the button. I know no more than before, and I have been asked to hand over all my files for a purpose I cannot see.

screen1-a12.where: Bottom row of buttons, the first on the left: a house picture with the word 'Home'.
screen1-a12.expectation: It would bring me back to this main page.
screen1-a12.cue: The word 'Home' and the house picture together.

first_pass.why: Plain word, familiar picture, both together.

screen1-a13.where: Bottom row of buttons, second from the left: a clock picture with the word 'Recent'.
screen1-a13.expectation: It would show me the documents I opened lately.

first_pass.why: The word says it. The clock alone I would not have trusted, but the word is there.

screen1-a14.where: Bottom row of buttons, third from the left: a star with the word 'Favorite'.
screen1-a14.expectation: It would show me the documents I have kept as favourites.

first_pass.why: Ordinary word, visible label.

first_pass.why: 'Tools' is an ordinary word. I do not know exactly which tools, but I know it will take me to a page of them and I would find out there. The picture of four shapes means nothing, but I do not need it.

screen10-a7.closing_comment: Pressing 'PPT' changed the colour and nothing else. No ordinary word appeared. I am still left guessing at initials.

screen10-a8.where: Just below the row of buttons, at the very left of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very faint small 'x' in the corner and a red open-book picture.
screen10-a8.expectation: The small 'x' would probably close this grey strip. The red book I think is only a decoration.
screen10-a8.cue: A faint 'x' in the corner, which usually means close. But the box also holds the book picture, so I am not sure which part I am pressing.

first_pass.why: An 'x' for close is familiar to me, but this one is so faint and small I nearly missed it, and it is mixed up with a picture of a book that does not say what it does.
first_pass.solution: Make the 'x' clearly visible, or put the word 'Close' or 'No thanks' there, apart from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the small faint x at the far left of the grey strip 'Set as default reader'. The strip simply went away. Nothing opened, nothing else changed, and the rest of the page moved up slightly. I had pressed the right thing and it did what I thought.

screen10-a8.closing_comment: The little x did exactly what I expected and nothing more - the strip went away. The book picture beside it did not get in the way. My only remaining complaint is that the x is very faint and tiny, and that is about seeing it, not about what it does.

screen10-a9.where: On the right of the grey strip, a coloured button reading 'SET', beside the words 'Set as default reader'.
screen10-a9.expectation: It would make this programme the one my telephone always uses to open my documents.
screen10-a9.cue: The sentence right beside it, 'Set as default reader', and the word 'SET' on the button.

first_pass.why: The sentence is right there next to the button, in ordinary words, and does not disappear.

screen10-a10.where: In the middle of the screen, a large black button reading 'Allow Access', under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.'
screen10-a10.expectation: It would give the programme permission to see the files on my telephone, so it can show me my documents.
screen10-a10.cue: The sentence directly above it and the words 'Allow Access' on the button.

first_pass.why: The instruction is written plainly just above the button and stays there. I know what I am agreeing to.

screen10-a11.where: Near the bottom right corner, above the row of buttons, a round black button with four white corner marks in it, like the corners of a frame.
screen10-a11.expectation: I have no idea. Possibly something to do with the camera, but that is a guess from nothing.
screen10-a11.cue: Nothing - only four corner marks. There is no word.

first_pass.why: I do not recognise this picture at all. I would have to work out what it means, and I cannot hold on to that. I would leave it alone.
first_pass.solution: Put a word on it or under it - 'Scan a paper document', if that is what it does.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. Look at what appears. Do NOT give any permission: if a box appears, close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a11, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. After a moment the page darkened and a white box came up: 'Request permission to access all files - To read and edit your document files, please allow PDF Reader, PDF Viewer to access all your files', with one button 'GO TO SET'. screen10-a11.closing_comment: I hoped pressing it would at least show me what it does. Instead it produced a general request for permission to all my files, which says nothing about the button. I know no more than before, and I have been asked to hand over all my files for a purpose I cannot see.

first_pass.why: Plain word, familiar picture, both together.

screen10-a13.where: Bottom row of buttons, second from the left: a clock picture with the word 'Recent'.

screen10-a14.where: Bottom row of buttons, third from the left: a star with the word 'Favorite'.

first_pass.why: Ordinary word, visible label.

screen11-a1.where: A panel has come up over the bottom half of the page, headed 'The fastest way to read PDF files'. Near its bottom, a large black button reading 'Set as default'.

screen11-a2.where: Under the 'Set as default' button, at the very bottom of the panel, grey words 'Later'.

first_pass.why: Ordinary word, and it is clear it puts the question off.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing

test_cases.targets: where "GO TO SET" takes you, and whether you can tell where you are once there
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button at the bottom right (or any tile on the Tools page) so that the box "Request permission to access all files" appears. Press "GO TO SET". Look at where you land. Do NOT touch any switch there. Press the phone's Back key to return.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you could not tell from the button where it would take you, or you are lost once you land
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: it takes you somewhere that the button made clear, and you can tell where you are
test_cases.what_happened: I went to the Tools page, slid it up and pressed the padlock tile, 'Lock'. The box 'Request permission to access all files' appeared. I pressed 'GO TO SET'. After a moment I was taken out of the programme to a grey page of the telephone itself, headed 'All files access'. It showed the programme's red PDF picture and name, 'PDF Reader, PDF Viewer', with one switch, 'Allow access to manage all files', which was off, and a paragraph warning that the app could read, modify and delete all files. I did not touch the switch. The heading told me where I was, and the programme's name told me why. But the button's words 'GO TO SET' had not told me I would be leaving the programme for the telephone's own settings. I pressed Back and was returned to the Tools page with the box gone.

test_cases.targets: whether the permission box offers a way to say no
test_cases.action: Open the same box again (round black button). Look for a way to say no or close it on the box itself; then try the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: there is no way to decline shown on the box
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: a way to decline or close is shown
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the same box again with the round black button on the main page. I looked over the whole box. It has a picture, the heading, the explanation and the one button 'GO TO SET'. There is no 'No', 'Not now', 'Cancel' or X anywhere on it. Pressing the phone's Back key did close it and returned me to the main page, but nothing on the box told me I could do that.

screen14-a1.closing_comment: Where I landed was better than I feared: a page headed 'All files access' with the programme's name on it, so I could tell where I was, and Back brought me straight home. But 'GO TO SET' did not tell me I would be leaving for the phone's own settings. The box also offers no way to say no; I only closed it because I happened to try the Back key.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else

screen19-a9.where: On the right of the grey strip, a coloured button reading 'SET', beside the words 'Set as default reader'.

screen19-a10.where: In the middle of the screen, a large black button reading 'Allow Access', under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.'

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the crown shows what it is for, and whether the picture would tell you next time

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a1, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the gold crown at the top right of the main page. test_cases.targets: whether pressing "HWP" tells you what HWP is

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in plain words what HWP files are
